title: Latin-script names — ICAO Doc 9303 §6.A folding to A–Z (single-letter option)
authority: ICAO Doc 9303, Machine Readable Travel Documents, 8th ed. (2021), Part 3 §6.A 'Transliteration of multinational Latin-based characters' (consolidated with Amendments 1–2)
description: Removes diacritics from Latin-script names the way machine-readable zones do: every row of the ICAO §6.A table, taking the single-letter option where ICAO offers one (Ä→A, Å→A, Ö→O, Ü→U, Ñ→N), plus Æ→AE, Ø→OE, Œ→OE, Þ→TH, Ĳ→IJ, ẞ/ß→SS, Đ/Ð→D, Ł→L. Wałęsa → Walesa, ĐOKOVIĆ → DOKOVIC.
notes: ICAO publishes upper-case rows only (95 rows, U+00C0–U+017D plus U+1E9E); keys here are their lower-case forms and the engine restores case. İ (U+0130) is aliased to I because its lower case is i + U+0307.

Where ICAO offers alternatives the single-letter option is used: Ä 'AE or A' → A, Å 'AA or A' → A, Ö 'OE or O' → O, Ü 'UE or UXX or U' → U, Ñ 'N or NXX' → N. latin_icao_digraph selects AE/AA/OE/UE. UXX and NXX (App. B §B.4.1, e.g. CAÑON → CANXXON) are not produced.
Ð (Eth, U+00D0) → D per ICAO; English Wikipedia's 'DH' alternative is not in the ICAO table. Đ (U+0110, printed with the Ð glyph) → D; the English convention dj is in sh_latn_ascii.

Letters ICAO omits, added here: Ə/ə → A (dominant Azerbaijani practice, Məmmədov → Mammadov; E is also seen in older spellings, Memmedov); Ș/Ț comma-below → S/T like the cedilla forms; digraph code points Ǆ/ǅ/ǆ → DZ/Dz/dz, Ǉ/ǈ/ǉ → LJ/Lj/lj, Ǌ/ǋ/ǌ → NJ/Nj/nj, Ǳ/ǲ/ǳ → DZ/Dz/dz (title-case forms via aliases); Macedonian scholarly Ǵ/Ḱ → G/K; Ʒ/ʒ and Ǯ/ǯ (ezh, Skolt Sami) → Z.

Lower-case ß is the lower case of the ICAO row ẞ → SS (Groß → Gross, GROẞ → GROSS); ı (dotless i) → I is an ICAO row. Ĳ/ĳ is aliased to two letters so that Dutch capitalisation is kept (Ĳsbrand → IJsbrand). Engine limitation: lower-case ß inside an otherwise upper-case word (GROß) yields 'ss' (GROss), because ß has no upper-case status; GROẞ gives GROSS.

Modifier-letter and typographic apostrophes (ʻ U+02BB, ʼ U+02BC, ’ U+2019, ‘ U+2018) become the ASCII apostrophe ' rather than being deleted (Oʻzbekiston → O'zbekiston), so VIZ-style output keeps them; the ICAO MRZ rule (apostrophes omitted, D'ARTAGNAN → DARTAGNAN) belongs to the MRZ formatter.
Characters not in the table (Vietnamese ơ/ư/ễ, other combining sequences) are folded by Unicode decomposition (fallback 'ascii'), so the output is always ASCII.

National MRZ practice that agrees: Poland strips diacritics (BACHLEDA<CURUS); Montenegro Đ→D, Ž→Z, Ć→C, Č→C, Š→S. German-speaking and Nordic issuers typically use the digraph options (latin_icao_digraph).
